summary: Invoice spike after private-deploy egress outage caused duplicate tool-invoke postbacks
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a 3x unexpected invoice increase for the billing period starting 2026-02-28. BrightMap's invoice shows duplicated line items labeled 'tool-invoke' and 'async-postback' for a 6-hour window on 2026-03-05. Impact: immediate billing overage and accounting reconciliation failure for finance team. Environment: BrightMap runs a Private deployment (VPC) in us-west-2 with a hosted fallback configured for egress outages. Observed behavior: during a transient egress outage (VPN tunnel flap) the private deployment routed traffic to hosted fallback; multiple postbacks from the tool-invoke worker queue were retried and recorded twice by the postback-reconciler, resulting in duplicate metering events that rolled into finalized invoice lines. Expected behavior: fallbacks should not cause duplicate metering; reconciler should deduplicate by postback fingerprint and idempotency token. BrightMap believes this is a billing-system bug and requests a provisional credit and details for audit.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a Private deployment with hosted fallback enabled for egress failures.
2) Trigger a short VPN tunnel outage (~5-10 minutes) to force fallback routing for in-flight tool-invoke requests.
3) Ensure tool-invoke worker is configured to use async postbacks with retry=3 and no jitter to simulate burst retries.
4) Observe postback-reconciler logs and billing events for duplicate fingerprints and duplicated invoice lines.

comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Customer submitted billing export and CSV of duplicated invoice lines; asked for provisional credit while we investigate.

2026-03-11 Liam O'Connor: Assigned for triage. Initial hypothesis: reconciler idempotency check failed when postbacks arrived from different gateway (private vs hosted) because fingerprint namespace includes gateway-id. Reproducing locally with unit test.
2026-03-11 SRE (Anika Rao): Confirmed brief VPN flap at 2026-03-05T10:12Z; routing table switch triggered fallback for ~8s. No other incidents reported in region.

2026-03-12 Billing (Marco Ruiz): Found two invoice lines created from separate billing events pbk-9f3d and pbk-9f3e. Both reference the same tool invocation fingerprint but different postback IDs. We can issue a provisional credit pending reconciler fix.
2026-03-12 Customer (BrightMap, J. Alvarez): Appreciates quick triage; requests detailed postmortem and assurance this won't recur. Asks for timeline for credit and permanent fix.
investigation_notes: Idempotency investigation: reconciler dedupe key currently uses (fingerprint, gateway-id, timestamp-window). When gateway-id differs (private vs hosted) dedupe fails even if fingerprint identical.
Root cause hypothesis: during fallback, postback retried from hosted path assigned a new postback_id and gateway-id, so reconciler treated as distinct event and emitted separate billing_event.
Reproducer: integration test created that forces postbacks with identical fingerprint but different gateway-id; billing_event duplication reproduced consistently.

Temporary mitigation considered: billboard a patch to reconciler to ignore gateway-id when fingerprint matches and timestamp delta < 1 minute for tool-invoke events; need sign-off from billing to avoid deduping legitimately distinct events.
Edge cases: system must not merge two unrelated events that happen to hash-collide fingerprint; add a secondary check using invocation_id and api_key when present.
Related code: postback-reconciler service and billing-processor pipeline. See PR attempt: https://github.com/redwood-inference/postback-reconciler/pull/842 (WIP)
Potential customer impact: invoice overcharge during short egress incidents where retries cross gateways; frequency low but high-dollar customers affected when tool-invokes are high-volume.
next_steps: 1) Issue provisional credit for duplicated invoice lines for BrightMap and notify finance (assigned: Marco Ruiz).
2) Merge reconciler patch to change dedupe key logic for tool-invoke events (owner: postback team).
3) Add integration test to prevent regressions for fallback scenarios (owner: QA).
4) Schedule postmortem with BrightMap and internal teams; publish runbook updates for private-hosted fallback accounting (owner: Support / SRE).
5) Monitor billing events for similar duplicates across enterprise customers for 72 hours after deploy.
